data.outcome_summary: This OECD country notes report summarizes results from the Survey of Adult Skills 2023 for Canada, covering adults aged 16–65 in three domains: literacy, numeracy, and adaptive problem solving. The assessment is administered exclusively on digital tablets and estimates proficiency on 500-point scales, with proficiency levels derived from task success/failure; the notes report mean scores, proficiency-level distributions (e.g., shares at Level 1 or below and at Levels 4–5), and uncertainty via 95% confidence intervals. The report also documents trends versus the 2011–12 cycle, including stability in literacy and an increase in numeracy, and discusses subgroup differences by age, educational attainment, gender, and immigrant background. Associations with economic and social outcomes are presented descriptively and with controls (e.g., a one-standard-deviation increase in numeracy proficiency relates to higher labour-force participation and wages), but no machine-learning modeling, PV-handling, or missing-data strategy is specified in the excerpt. The “doorstep” questionnaire is used for respondents with insufficient assessment-language fluency and is generally excluded from cross-cycle comparisons to preserve comparability.
